source_of_truth: Executed notebook outputs. Every number below is transcribed from a cell output in Notebooks/, never from memory.
_note_counts_verified: Unique-JD counts were measured directly from the CSVs on 2026-07-27. Earlier versions of this file reported 200 and 305; the true values are 150 and 255. See docs/DATA_CARD.md.

training_v2.composition: strict superset of training_v1: 500 'original' rows (150 JDs) + 315 'expansion' rows (105 new JDs)

notebook_01_baselines_internal_test_50_p._scope: 500-pair training set; internal test drawn from the same 150 postings as training. Diagnostic only.
notebook_01_baselines_internal_test_50_p.finding: Fine-tuning roughly doubled MPNet's ranking quality and made every model's MAE worse — the calibration gap, which notebook 02 investigates.

notebook_02_architecture_internal_test_5._scope: 500-pair training set, internal test. See the caveat cell in the notebook: training is unseeded and this run drew an unlucky MPNet.
notebook_02_architecture_internal_test_5.seed_variance_warning: MPNet fine-tuned scores 0.8444 in notebook 01 and 0.8516 in notebook 03 under an identical configuration. The ~0.28 Spearman spread is run-to-run training noise; these notebooks seed the split but not training. Notebook 05 uses 3 seeds with mean +/- std for this reason.
notebook_02_architecture_internal_test_5.finding: Isotonic calibration cut bi-encoder MAE by ~37-38% while leaving Spearman essentially unchanged. That result holds for both bi-encoders and does not depend on which model won.

notebook_03_external_validation._scope: 500-pair training set. The notebook that changed the project's direction.

DeBERTa-v3 cross-encoder.note: Spearman undefined — near-constant predictions; the classifier head never learned to discriminate

notebook_03_external_validation.headline_finding: The RoBERTa cross-encoder won the internal test (0.8917 vs 0.8516) and inverted on unseen postings (-0.6122) — a 1.50 Spearman swing. 125M parameters on 400 examples is ~312k parameters per example; it memorized the training postings. The calibrated bi-encoder lost only 0.076 Spearman across the same transfer.
notebook_03_external_validation.hybrid_note: The 'Hybrid' rows in this notebook duplicate the cross-encoder rows exactly: at 1:1 scoring the hybrid delegates to the cross-encoder and inherits its failure completely.

notebook_04_overfitting_fixes_external_t._scope: 500-pair training set. Four anti-overfitting fixes ablated, evaluated externally only.
notebook_04_overfitting_fixes_external_t.conclusion: Every fix helped (-0.35 -> +0.51 external Spearman) and none beat the simple calibrated bi-encoder at 0.77. At this data scale, cross-encoder capacity is a liability.

notebook_05_production._status: VALID. Re-run 2026-07-29 with the save_best_model fix; every number below describes models/seed43, the checkpoint that was saved.
notebook_05_production._fix: SentenceTransformer.fit() defaults to save_best_model=True, so output_path holds the best-by-validation checkpoint while the in-memory model is the final epoch. The first run calibrated and measured the in-memory model and published the directory — different weights, mismatched calibrator, and a silently wrong audit. Notebook 05 and src/train.py now reload from output_path before calibrating, so the calibrator, the metrics and the artifact are the same object.
notebook_05_production.run: 3 seeds (42/43/44), 815 pairs / 255 postings, combined CoSENT + CosineSimilarity loss, 22 min/seed on a T4

fine_tuning_delta.note: vs base all-mpnet-base-v2 on the identical 106 held-out pairs

precision_at_1.note: 53 unseen postings, 4 candidates each; ranking is calibration-invariant so raw cosine is used

notebook_05_production._seed_spread: 0.8186-0.8538 Spearman across three seeds of an identical recipe. Reported as mean +/- std because notebook 02 showed a single run of this pipeline swings ~0.28 at this data scale.
notebook_05_production._not_yet_published: The publish cell has not been executed, so the Hub still serves a 2026-07-27 checkpoint. Until it runs, notebook 06 audits the wrong weights and scripts/build_demo_data.py refuses to bundle the fine-tuned engine.

claude_opus_4_5_external_final_test_106_.setup: Same 106-pair external final test as the fine-tuned model. Production system+user prompt, schema-constrained JSON, one call per pair, zero-shot, no extended thinking (this Bedrock model rejects it) — a matched floor, not Claude's ceiling.
claude_opus_4_5_external_final_test_106_.takeaway: Calibration is monotonic, so Spearman is unchanged while MAE drops from 0.25 to 0.16 — most of Claude's absolute-error gap was calibration, not judgment. Reproduce: scripts/claude_benchmark.py + scripts/calibrate.py.
claude_opus_4_5_external_final_test_106_._comparison_note: Compare against the fine-tuned model's numbers in notebook_05_production above, on the identical 106 pairs.

audit._status: QUARANTINED — audited the stale Hub checkpoint, not models/seed43.
audit._evidence: The audit measured raw Spearman 0.7891 (cosine range [0.569, 0.890]) — bit-identical across two audit runs while notebook 05's model changed from 0.8173 to 0.8340. The HF repo's lastModified is 2026-07-27, predating both production runs, and platt_calibrator.pkl 404s there. The audit paired a fresh local calibrator with stale Hub weights: the worst possible combination.

tfidf.note: MAE omitted: TF-IDF cosine is not an estimate of the 0-1 label; only ranking is comparable

_valid_regardless._why: None of these depend on the published fine-tuned model.

audit._guards: Notebook 06 aborts on a >0.01 raw-Spearman disagreement with production_results.json; notebook 05's export cell now re-downloads the Hub model and reports whether the publish actually happened; scripts/build_demo_data.py refuses mismatched predictions (it rejected this run's).
